about: Starter rule pack. It explains the warnings the game writes when a save was made with other versions of scripts (a mod was updated or removed), and the warning that the script engine is overloaded. Its rules are explain rules, so a match shows as FOUND and never fails a run.
source: The wording follows the Creation Kit wiki page 'Papyrus Runtime Errors' and the lines Starfield writes to Papyrus.0.log.

explain.re: differs from the in-game resource files - using version from save
explain.means: The save was made while a function was running, and that function has changed since then (the mod was updated). The game finishes the old version from the save first. It is a sign that you are testing on an old save.

explain.re: doesn't exist in the in-game resource files - using version from save
explain.means: The save was made while a function was running, and that function no longer exists in the script on disk. The game finishes the old version from the save.

explain.re: Unable to get type \S+ referenced by the save game
explain.means: The save holds objects of a script that no longer exists or didn't load. Usually a mod that was removed or renamed its scripts. Those objects are not loaded.

explain.re: Type of variable \S+ on script \S+, which is \S+, doesn't match the type loaded
explain.means: A script variable changed type between the save and now. The saved value is thrown away.

explain.re: loaded from save not found within the actual object
explain.means: The save holds a script variable that the script no longer has. The saved value is thrown away. This is normal after a mod update.
The script engine was too busy and wrote a dump of every running script. Look in the dump for one script that appears many times: it may be running away (a loop or an update that never stops).
